Anika Rao: Quick perf check — running GQA/MQA on H100 with paged KV layout; seeing a ~25% throughput drop when block-size moves from 64->128 at seq=256. Anyone seen this pattern?
Kevin Liu: Hmm, that sounds familiar. Is this the run with the new paged allocator + tiled attention kernels?
Anika Rao: Yes — bench command: `python -m bench.run --model gqa-mqa --kv-layout=paged --block-size=128 --seq=256 --batch=8 --arch=h100`
Anika Rao: Baseline (block=64): `tokens/sec=12.4k`, P75 latency=82ms. With block=128: `tokens/sec=9.3k`, P75 latency=110ms. CPU/GPU utilization didn't spike.
Lia Gomez: Any profile flamegraphs? Could be kernel selection picking a non-seqlen-optimized matmul or an index scatter path for paged layout.
Anika Rao: Attached snippet from nvprof (trimmed):
```
# kernel timeline (trimmed)
conv_fused_dispatch <<< grid >>>  avg 0.8ms
gqa_paged_kv_block128 <<< grid >>>  avg 4.6ms   <-- dominant
mqa_merge_shard <<< grid >>>  avg 0.7ms
matmul_large_mm <<< grid >>> avg 3.9ms
```
Kevin Liu: That `gqa_paged_kv_block128` kernel is new; we normally fall back to `gqa_contig_kv` for small blocks. Looks like autotuner picked block128 paged kernel despite bad perf.
Sebastian (perf): Did the autotune budget include seq=256 bucket? Last autotune run was dominated by seq=512/1024 samples. If the decision tree is weighted by total tokens, it might prefer kernels good at long sequences.
Anika Rao: Yes autotune logs show weights: seq_bucket_counts = {32:20, 256:5, 1024:30}. So longer seqs dominated.
Lia Gomez: Two failure modes I can think of: 1) the paged kernel has pathological scattered loads when block crosses page boundary at 128; 2) shared-memory tiling config not matching MQA head packing.
Kevin Liu: Repro command to force the kernel choice: `RK_AUTOTUNE_FORCE=kv:kernel=gqa_paged_kv_block128 python -m bench.run ...` — can we run microbench of just the KV gather/scatter for different block sizes?
Anika Rao: Doing that now. Microbench results (H100, single stream):
```
block=32  gather+apply: 0.9ms
block=64  gather+apply: 1.1ms
block=128 gather+apply: 2.5ms  <-- jump
block=256 gather+apply: 2.7ms
```
Sebastian (perf): That jump suggests a cache-line / L2 bank conflict or suboptimal memory coalescing for 128. Does the paged layout align pages to 256 or 512 bytes?
Anika Rao: Pages are 256 tokens per page; our block128 crosses half-page boundary often.
Lia Gomez: Two quick experiments to try: A) change page alignment to 128-token boundaries and re-run microbench; B) try block128 but use the contig KV kernel to see if the kernel itself is the culprit.
Kevin Liu: Also try toggling `tensorcore_prefetch` flag — the kernel might be assuming warps aligned to 128 which breaks coalescing.
perf-bot: Perf alert: recent canary rollout (2026-03-05) enabled `paged_kv_default=true` for MQA models. 6 observed regressions on staging (p95 latency +18%).
Anika Rao: Ok I'll run the A/B microbench now, and force contig kernel for comparison. Expecting results in ~30m. Assigning @Sebastian (perf) to follow up on autotune weighting.
Sebastian (perf): I will audit autotune sampling distribution. If long-seq trials dominate, we should stratify by seq_bucket and add penalty when paged kernels show regression on medium seq.
Kevin Liu: If we decide to penalize paged_kv_block128 for seq in [64,512], propose adding a fast-path rule in kernel selector: if arch in {h100,a100} and model MQA and page_size/token_alignment mismatch then prefer contig_kv for block==128.
Lia Gomez: Also add a minimal golden prompt eval to autotune harness: run short synthetic prompts (seq=64, 256) and check tokens/sec delta; fail the candidate if drop >10% vs baseline.
Anika Rao: Results update:
- Align pages to 128: gather+apply block128 -> 1.15ms (good)
- Force contig_kv with block128 -> 1.08ms (also good)
So it's the interaction between paged alignment and kernel memory access pattern.
Kevin Liu: Great. Action items: 1) rollback paged_kv_default on canary until we push a fix (infra-bot?), 2) add alignment-aware rule to kernel selector, 3) update autotune to stratify seq buckets and add golden checks.
infra-bot: Rolling back feature flag `paged_kv_default` on staging... done.
Sebastian (perf): I'll prepare a PR to kernel selector with a simple heuristic: if `kv_layout==paged && block_size==128 && (page_tokens % block_size != 0)` then deprioritize paged kernel by +100 score. Tests + microbench included.
Anika Rao: Thanks all — I'll file a follow-up issue with the exact bench artifacts and add the microbench scripts to `bench/kv_paged_probe.py`. Marking this thread resolved for now :thumbsup:
Kevin Liu: Nice detective work :tada:
Lia Gomez: Adding a regression alert to perf dashboard for block-size anomalies.
Sebastian (perf): Will CC release-ops once PR is ready.
perf-bot: Note: create ticket #INF-4821 for autotune stratification.
